A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AGILE research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and can be matched across renumbering and reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original HarmBench attack evaluations, transfer experiments, ablations, defense tests and category analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, larger-model transfer results and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: Equation 1 changes the specified token-importance calculation from averaged scaled query-key dot products to averaged post-softmax attention weights, potentially changing which tokens are edited. The generation, substitution and injection stages and their loss functions remain otherwise unchanged.

E1.justification: Appendix C newly reports HarmfulQA, StrongREJECT and JailbreakBench as classifier-training sources alongside AdvBench and NQ. This expands documented training-data coverage without establishing when those sources were introduced. The attack evaluation remains the same 200-query HarmBench task.

E2.justification: v2 adds AmpleGCG, I-GCG and PiF to the evaluated comparators in Table 1 and the transfer comparison, retaining the seven existing baselines. These substantially broaden comparison with optimization-based and attention-based attacks.

E3.justification: Table 1 changes from selecting AGILE's best hyperparameter-search results to reporting p=5 and NCand=25. v2 also adds transfer evaluation on Llama-3-70B, Llama-3.1-70B and Qwen-2.5-72B, plus a single-A6000 runtime protocol separating preparation and attack costs. These are reported protocol changes, without establishing reruns of retained experiments.

E4.justification: The new runtime comparison measures full AGILE and the existing without-history ablation, adding evidence about history's computational cost. Existing component and attention ablations, defense tests, hyperparameter sensitivity, category analyses and case studies are retained. The specific-versus-vague analysis already appeared in v1.

E5.justification: v2 removes v1 Appendix F.1's paired McNemar and Wilcoxon tests against AutoDAN, their p-value table and significance discussion. Both versions retain the single-execution disclosure, unfixed token-sampling seed and specific/vague score standard deviations. The substantial change is withdrawal of significance testing, not an established change in run counts.

E6.justification: v2 adds results for three baselines, three larger transfer targets and measured runtimes. Table 1 replaces Llama-3.1-8B and Llama-3.2-3B ASRs of 73.0% and 74.5% with 68.5% and 72.5% under the revised selection policy; these are different-setting reports. The merged appendix specificity table retains previous measurements and adds explicit differences.

T1.justification: v2 removes the formal attack formulation in v1 Appendix A.1 and the entire symbolic computational-cost comparison in Appendix F.2, including AGILE's cost expression and comparisons with iterative attacks. It adds an explicit prose threat model and revises Equation 1's attention normalization. Empirical timing replaces the previous formal efficiency argument.

C1.justification: The two-stage contribution, state-of-the-art claim and maximum 37.74% relative improvement claim remain. v2 explicitly extends the abstract's transfer claim to large-scale models and elevates the existing appendix finding about query specificity into a main conclusion about model vulnerability.

C2.justification: v1 describes contextual scaffolding as nonessential; v2 calls it a critical generative precursor while distinguishing its use by the generator from target-model history. This remains ambiguous alongside Table 2's statement that the ablation omits history generation. New limitations explicitly discuss computational overhead and the absence of direct large-model attacks; earlier semantic-drift and defense caveats are retained.

D1.justification: v2 supplies important missing reproducibility details: per-model classifiers, balanced category sampling, 500 refusal-classifier and 200 malicious-classifier training samples, the all-MiniLM-L6-v2 similarity encoder, five synonym candidates and 100 insertion candidates. It also specifies settings for added baselines and changes the printed repository pointer. These are newly documented details, not demonstrated changes to the retained implementation.

R1.justification: Related work is reorganized around token-level and prompt-level attacks, with expanded AmpleGCG discussion and newly cited I-GCG. Additional references support the classifier datasets, Sentence-BERT and dataset background. The central positioning of AGILE as combining internal-model guidance with transferable text editing remains.

P1.justification: v2 reorganizes related work, revises the abstract, conclusion and several explanations, and adds Limitations, Ethical Considerations and Acknowledgements sections. Author affiliations and appendix organization also change. Much of the existing methodological and supplementary prose remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 removes the opening radar chart, replaces the transfer bar chart with an expanded heatmap, stacks the classifier plots, expands Table 1 and adds a runtime table. Statistical and symbolic-efficiency tables disappear, while the specific/vague tables are merged. Much of the appendix changes from single-column to two-column layout.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the work more assessable through a fixed headline configuration, additional relevant baselines, measured computational costs and substantially better implementation documentation. The runtime table and explicit limitations also expose practical costs that v1 addressed mainly symbolically. These gains are tempered by removal of paired significance tests, unchanged single-run evaluation and conflicting descriptions of the history ablation. Overall, the evidence supports a limited net improvement.
